The Table 4 caption names only DASS-21 (stress), but the table reports depression, anxiety and stress scales.
The authors report a significant reduction in pain catastrophizing factors although they state that no inferential statistical tests were applied.
The authors attribute improvements to the intervention in places but state that the uncontrolled A–B design does not allow causal inference and other factors may have contributed.

The intervention was grounded in cognitive–behavioral therapy (CBT) and its four core principles [], with the aim of promoting psychological well-being, enhancing treatment adherence, increasing self-efficacy, and optimizing recovery.
Psychological intervention began on 13 December and continued until 30 June.
The intervention was structured into 15 sessions (Table 1)
with a follow-up session held three months after medical discharge
Sessions lasted approximately 50 min

primarily conducted in person at a room in the Faculty of Psychology at a university, although some were delivered online due to logistical reasons (academic, travel, work or rehabilitation constraints)
The session format typically included: 10 min for reviewing updates and homework, 10 min of theoretical explanation, 25 min of guided practice, and a final 5 min to set new tasks
Goals were formulated for the short, medium, and long term, and were explicit, measurable, achievable, and positively framed.
Both performance goals (e.g., completing a specific number of rehabilitation exercises) and outcome goals (e.g., walking unaided) were included, with prioritization of performance goals
the introduction of attention focuses was intended to enhance the player’s ability to direct her attention both to bodily sensations and to her thoughts
Relaxation strategies included diaphragmatic breathing [] and the “Body Scan” technique from the Mindfulness approach
the “Body Scan” technique from the Mindfulness approach [], aimed at emotional regulation, pain management, and enhancing general well-being
it was complemented with sleep hygiene and stimulus control strategies [], such as avoiding screen use before bedtime, maintaining consistent sleep schedules, and limiting long naps
Active coping skills and problem-solving abilities were also trained to minimize the impact of concerns about rest and well-being
the cognitive reappraisal of the injury event as a challenge rather than a threat
a writing technique was implemented based on the work of Mankad and Gordon [], focused on the “letter to the injury”
Cognitive restructuring was approached through the use of A-B-C thought records (activating event, belief, emotional/behavioral consequence)
Additional techniques included thought-stopping
behavioral and cognitive distraction strategies
the so-called “worry time”, in which the athlete dedicated a specific time of day to process recurring concerns
visualization was used at various stages of the process []. Initially, it served as tool for relaxation and well-being.

it was used as an imagined practice to accompany more complex exercises in the physical and sports rehabilitation process, with the aim of strengthening the athlete’s confidence and reducing the fear of reinjury

Psychological assessment was online and conducted at four key time points: initial evaluation, follow-up during rehabilitation, medical discharge, and follow-ups at three- and six-month post-discharge.
During the initial evaluation, the following instruments were administered: VAS, FMPS, STAI, POMS, BDI-II, PCS, and PSQI.
During the follow-up phase, the VAS, PCS, POMS, DASS-21, GHQ-12 and PSQI were re-administered.
At the time of medical discharge, the DASS-21, GHQ-12, PSQI and PRIA-RS were used
the subsequent follow-ups included repeated assessments using the POMS, DASS-21, GHQ-12 and PSQI
A semi-structured interview was conducted to collect information on sociodemographic variables and the context of the sports injury

The player’s first matches were recorded in a similar way to the recording method used by Palmi et al. []. The match, results, performance rating (Likert scale from 0 = very low to 10 = very high), emotional state and the player’s observations were taken into account
